video.title: The Laziest AI Side Hustle Anyone Can Start Right Now

summary: Chris Koerner pitches a low-effort AI side hustle: cloning a realtor's voice with Fish Audio S2 Pro and generating pre-written voicemails in the languages of multilingual buyers, sold for about $200-500 a month. He demos the workflow (clone voice from a 17-second sample, draft scripts with an LLM, translate, generate audio, save to Google Drive) and claims it costs cents per message. He then lists adjacent ideas (audiobook narration, YouTube dubbing, local-business voiceover, other multilingual professions) and a day-by-day plan to land the first clients. Key takeaway: cheap voice-cloning tools let a solo operator sell a productised service, but the claims are hypothetical and the video promotes an affiliate-style code for Fish Audio.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; presents the idea solo and demos the tool.

ideas.name: Multilingual cloned-voice voicemails for realtors
ideas.one_liner: Clone a realtor's voice and supply a library of translated voicemail templates in the languages of their multilingual leads, on a monthly subscription.
ideas.business_model: Monthly retainer/subscription plus optional setup fee; possible free or one-off package as a foot-in-the-door.
ideas.customer: Real estate agents and brokerages in markets with many non-English-speaking buyers.
ideas.problem: Realtors cannot leave voicemails in other languages, and generic translation does not sound like them, so they lose speed-to-lead and trust with multilingual buyers.
ideas.offer: Clone the realtor's voice from a 30-60 second clip (or existing social video), then deliver a library of pre-recorded translated voicemails (new listing, price drop, showing confirmation, missed appointment, etc.) in the same voice.

pricing.model: Monthly recurring fee, optional setup fee, or one-time package as loss leader
pricing.notes: Suggests a one-time free or cheap package first to get a foot in the door, then upsell AI services.

acquisition_channels.details: Day 2: contact friends and contacts who are realtors by text or lunch, proactively clone their voice and show them the result; use their reviews as testimonials for strangers.

quote.text: Take them to lunch. Proactively clone their voice. Show them what you did at lunch so they can hear it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Visit broker offices with food and teach agents how to do it; leave a one-page flyer with QR code, pricing and URL; follow up repeatedly.
Collect five-star reviews and list on Google Business Profile after the first clients.
Proactively send pre-made sample audio files in the prospect's cloned voice before pitching (suggested as 'creepy but effective').

quote.text: Hey, I've got 40 audio files with your voice in four different languages of 10 different voicemails that you're using on a daily basis.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Operator clones the voice in Fish Audio, uses an LLM to write and translate 10 voicemail scripts, generates audio one message at a time per language, downloads and organises into Google Drive folders, and sends to the agent. About 20-40 minutes per new client.
unit_economics_claims: Fish Audio cost about $15 for 250,000 credits; the two demo clips used about 423 credits (about 3 cents or less).
Setup fees of $500-$1,000 per new client on top.
20-40 minutes of work per new client.
ideas.startup_cost: About $15 for Fish Audio credits (stated); no other costs stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Plan suggests first 3-5 clients in weeks 2-4.

acquisition.how: Friend outreach, lunches and visiting offices are human. Cold outreach to individual realtors (often sole traders) by SMS/DM/email is restricted under UK PECR; only inbound or limited-company email is feasible by software.

onboarding.how: Agent collects a voice clip or scrapes public video; consent and voice-rights capture can be a form flow, with human checks on consent.

delivery.how: LLM script writing, translation and TTS are scriptable via API, though the demo uses the UI one message at a time and a native speaker should check translations.

billing.how: Standard subscription billing via Stripe or similar.

support.how: Revision requests, re-recordings and translation complaints can be handled by an agent with human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Technology works the same, but the demand rests on US demographics and a US-style voicemail-driven realtor workflow. UK agents mostly use email and WhatsApp, and sending voicemails or automated marketing calls to leads is regulated by PECR and UK GDPR, and voice cloning needs documented consent. A UK version would target London and other multilingual markets and possibly other languages.

risks: Voice-cloning consent and misuse concerns (voice is a personal data and likeness issue).
Voicemails sound accented; translation quality is unverified without native speakers.
Marketing voicemails and calls to leads are regulated (PECR/TCPA-type rules).
Clients may do it themselves once they learn the tool.
Dependence on one vendor (Fish Audio) pricing and terms.

ideas.name: Voicemail localisation for other multilingual-client professions
ideas.one_liner: Sell the same cloned-voice multilingual voicemail service to insurance agents, car dealerships, lawyers, medical offices and especially immigration attorneys.
ideas.business_model: Monthly retainer plus setup fee, same as realtor offer.
ideas.customer: Insurance agents, car dealers, lawyers, medical offices, immigration attorneys.
ideas.problem: They serve multilingual clients but cannot leave voicemails in those languages in their own voice.
ideas.delivery: Same workflow as the realtor offer with different scripts.

acquisition.how: Cold email to limited-company firms is lawful in the UK, but individuals and sole traders are restricted.

uk_applicability.notes: Immigration solicitors and medical practices exist in the UK, but regulated professions (SRA, GDPR, medical data) add compliance concerns.

risks: Regulated professions may restrict use of AI voice and require consent and data safeguards.

quotes.text: an immigration attorney could be perfect for this. They've got money and they're only dealing with multilingual clients.

ideas.name: AI audiobook narration for indie authors
ideas.one_liner: Narrate authors' books in their own cloned voice with Fish Audio at a fraction of studio cost.
ideas.customer: Self-published authors without the time or budget for studio narration.
ideas.problem: Recording 12 hours of audio is time-consuming and professional narrators are expensive, while most books sell few copies.
ideas.offer: Audiobook narration in the author's cloned voice, meeting Audible-style specs, optionally in multiple languages.

pricing.notes: Author still saves versus thousands for a studio.

ideas.delivery: Upload the manuscript to the TTS tool using the author's cloned voice, then export audio files in the required format.
unit_economics_claims: $500 to a couple of thousand per book versus studio costs.

acquisition.how: Author directories and marketplaces such as Fiverr/Reedsy can drive inbound; cold outreach to sole-trader authors is restricted in the UK.

onboarding.how: Manuscript upload and voice sample via form.

delivery.how: Batch TTS pipeline with spot checks for pronunciation.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK, but Audible and ACX policies on AI-narrated audiobooks may restrict or require disclosure; check current rules.

risks: Platform rules on AI-narrated audiobooks may change.

quotes.text: They don't have the budget to pay a professional voice actor to do it. So, it's like boom, 500 bucks. I'll do it for you in your voice.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: YouTube dubbing and voice-clone service for creators
ideas.one_liner: Dub YouTubers' videos into multiple languages using their cloned voice so they can sell ads in other markets.
ideas.business_model: Per-project or retainer service for creators.
ideas.customer: YouTube channels, e.g. those with 100k-500k subscribers.
ideas.problem: Creators want multilingual audiences and ad revenue but dubbing takes a lot of work.
ideas.offer: Voice cloning and dubbing of videos into other languages.

acquisition_channels.details: Find the business email on each YouTube channel's About page, or buy YouTuber email lists via Upwork or onlinejobs.ph; niche down by channel size.

quote.text: Every YouTuber's email address is right there.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Transcribe, translate and generate dubbed audio in the creator's cloned voice, then deliver audio tracks.
unit_economics_claims: Koerner says he dubbed his own channels into 14 languages, which helps him sell ads in other countries.

acquisition.how: Cold email to channel business addresses is feasible, but UK PECR limits emails to sole-trader creators.

onboarding.how: Creator shares video access and a voice sample.

delivery.how: Pipeline of transcription, translation and TTS can be automated; alignment and QA need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Works globally; most creators are individuals so UK outreach rules apply.

risks: YouTube now offers native auto-dubbing, which may erode demand.
Sole-trader creators are restricted for UK cold email.

quotes.text: I dubbed my channels into 14 different languages and it helps me make more money because I'm able to sell ads in those other countries
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Build a voice-cloned voicemail pack
steps: Clone the realtor's voice in Fish Audio from a 10-60 second clip, or from existing Instagram/YouTube video.

Ask an LLM for 10 generic voicemail scripts (new listing, price reduction, showing confirmation, offer accepted, counter offer, inspection, closing reminder, anniversary, referral request, holiday check-in), each under 30 seconds.
Translate into target languages (Spanish, Vietnamese, Mandarin, Portuguese; also Hindi, Italian, German, French).
Generate audio per message and per language one at a time, since batch download merges them.
Organise in Google Drive folders per language and send.

quote.text: write 10 common real estate voicemail messages a realtor would leave for clients.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Proactive demo before pitching
steps: Clone the prospect's voice before the meeting, ideally from a public video.
Generate sample voicemails in several languages.
Offer to share the files, or generate them only after they say yes.

tactics.name: Free or one-time package as loss leader
steps: Offer a one-time package or do it free, costing a few dollars in credits.
Use it to start a conversation about other AI help (more leads, faster response, more listings).
Convert to recurring services.

quote.text: Why don't I do this for you for free? It might cost you like a couple bucks in credits.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: First 30-day launch plan
steps: Day 1: sign up, clone your own voice, make three demo voicemails in English, Spanish and Chinese.
Day 2: message friends who are real estate agents, take them to lunch and show a cloned demo.
Days 3-7: follow up with every office and friend.
Weeks 2-4: land 3-5 clients, over-deliver and deliver faster than promised, collect five-star reviews and list on Google Business Profile.
Month 2: expand to audiobooks, insurance agencies and immigration attorneys.

quote.text: Follow-up, follow-up, follow-up. That's where the magic is.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Teach-for-free at broker offices
steps: Bring lunch to a broker office and offer to teach agents something new with AI.
Show them how to do it themselves for free.
Leave a one-page flyer with QR code, pricing and URL.
Expect them to ask you to do it for them: give away the secrets, sell the implementation.

quote.text: Give away the secrets. Sell the implementation.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Niche down by channel size
steps: Pick a segment, such as YouTube channels with 100k-500k subscribers.
Offer voice cloning and dubbing only to them.

warnings.warning: The cloned voice speaking Spanish sounds like an English speaker with a foreign accent, not a native speaker, so quality and authenticity for real leads are unverified.

quote.text: That does not sound like I'm from Mexico or Spain or that I'm a native speaker at all.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Batch downloading in Fish Audio merges the messages, so each file must be downloaded individually.

quote.text: you need to do it one by one, not all together, or it will just combine them all.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Using friends' unpaid reviews as 'testimonials' without disclosure is ethically and legally questionable (UK CMA rules on fake and incentivised reviews).

quote.text: And they don't need to know that your testimonials are from your friends.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The speaker admits that translated verb conjugations and Mandarin could not be verified by him, so a native-speaker check is needed.

quote.text: I didn't conjugate the verbs perfectly, but just kidding. I have no idea what I'm listening to
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Reduce friction for the customer: scrape public video for the voice sample and do the work for them instead of asking them to record.

quote.text: the more friction we can remove from this process or any sales process, the better.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A cheap proactive demo made with the prospect's own assets (voice, listings) is a strong opener compared with a generic pitch.
Productise one capability (voice cloning) and re-skin it for adjacent verticals by changing scripts, rather than building new products.

quote.text: Same service, different script.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Give away the know-how and sell implementation; most professionals know it is possible but won't do it themselves.
Recurring revenue is attractive but buyers resist it, so a one-time package can be the door-opener before a retainer.

quote.text: We all want recurring, but people are less likely to pay for recurring.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Aggressive follow-up after initial contact is where conversions happen.

quote.text: Follow-up, follow-up, follow-up. That's where the magic is.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Very low marginal cost (cents per asset) with a $200-500 monthly price means margins are high, but defensibility is low since tools are public.
Start with warm contacts to obtain testimonials, then use them to close strangers.

quote.text: It's going to be much easier to close a stranger once you have some testimonials of your friends.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Single-host walkthrough with a real demo of the tool and cost, but all revenue figures are hypothetical, no customers are reported, and demand for the voicemail service is unvalidated. The anecdote about the junk removal founder is second-hand.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes Fish Audio with a code (kerner 20) and a description link, likely an affiliate or sponsor arrangement.
